agents.reasoning: Lane: skeptic. I read the 10-Q, the 10-K and six 2026 debt documents first. Amazon has gone from $65.6B of long-term debt (Dec-25) to ~$164B face by Sept-26, through USD, EUR, CHF, CAD and GBP issues with coupons up to 6.65% and maturities to 2076. It also signed a $17.5B delayed-draw term loan. TTM FCF is -$7.6B, $29.3B of capex was accrued but not yet paid, and Moody's cut the outlook to stable (external funding). The bigger red flag is circularity: Amazon put $50B into OpenAI and $10B into Anthropic in H1-26, and both labs made $100B+ AWS commitments. Meanwhile $62.8B of H1 pre-tax income came from Level 3 Anthropic mark-ups - so GAAP 2026 EPS ($12.88 consensus) overstates operating earnings; I value only the 2027-28 operating EPS and add the stakes at a 50% haircut. Fitzgerald calls the OpenAI framework 'circular financing'. Amazon also has a precedent of over-building, with the 2021-22 fulfillment glut (shareholder-suit record). Weighed honestly, though: the accounting critique (Burry) mostly spares Amazon, which shortened server lives to 5 years in 2025. Insider activity is routine RSU sales plus Bezos gifts, with no cluster selling. AWS re-accelerated to 37% with $496B of backlog, which rebuts DA Davidson's Feb 'losing the lead' downgrade. Credit is A1/AA with no covenants. So the skeptic case is about FCF quality and valuation, not solvency or fraud. On 12 peers (one MarketScreener basis, FY ending Jun-27 to May-28), AMZN is near the median P/E and below the median EV/EBITDA. Applying below-median multiples and a capex-file-based EPS haircut gives ~$296-300 for the multiple methods. A DCF at a market-implied 10.4% WACC gives only $144, which shows how much of the price rests on long-run margins and low discount rates. Blended fair value is $267 (+4%). Scenarios are $195/$265/$340 at 25/50/25, for an expected ~$266. The ladder blends that scenario mixture with a lognormal (median $262, sigma 0.34, close to the 34% realized vol), so P(>=$256) = 0.54. It is slightly less bullish than the multiple methods alone and well below the $330.59 street target, which I treat as evidence but not the answer. No option data was used.
